newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures drifted lower on Friday as weakness in the U.S. bond market prompted local traders to unwind positions ahead of a long weekend in France.
The bond future started the day in a relatively positive mood but few traders had expected it to make any independent moves and overseas markets provided the direction.

Traders also said they expected the contract to continue its range-bound existence next week with 127.00 setting a good psychological support and 127.80 remaining a target for the bulls. It settled at 127.20 on Friday, down 0.08.
"It's the French domestics, the locals who are selling it," said a trader at U.S. house in Paris. He said there was little news behind the move.

Another trader said the usual Friday-afternoon wave of rumours, ranging from French Prime Minister Juppe's resignation to the death of U.S. president Clinto, was washing round trading floors but with limited market impact.

The 10-year spread between French and German bonds moved to minus two from minus three basis points. The Treasury managed to sell another 1.7 billion francs of OATs, the TEC 10 once again proving to be the favoured instrument.

The current vogue for TEC 10 variable rate bonds prompted German borrower KFW International Finance to follow the European Investment Bank's lead and issue another TEC 10 linked 2006 French franc bond.

As was the case with the EIB bond, French domestic investors, notably insurance companies, were buyers of the instrument as they were attracted by the short term benefit of a 4.50 percent a floor on the coupon, syndicate managers said.
December PIBOR underperformed slightly, dropping four basis points and pushing the spread over the equivalent German contract to 35 from 32 on Thursday.
The franc slipped late in the day to 3.3820 per mark but remained in a relatively narrow range.
Call money was unchanged at 3-1/4 3/8 percent.
